A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReNF research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting benchmarks, component ablations, training dynamics, repeated-seed results, and empirical oracle-combination evaluations.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds short-term forecasting benchmarks and M4/PEMS ablation results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core recursive BDO architecture, ReNF variants, weighted time/frequency loss, and EMA procedure remain unchanged. For M4, v5 explicitly makes every intermediate forecast cover the full horizon, disabling the short-to-long curriculum while retaining forecast combination (Appendix E.1). This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v5 retains the eight long-term benchmarks and adds evaluations on CarSales, Power, METR-LA, Website, SP500, NASDAQ, PEMS03/08, and M4 Yearly/Quarterly/Monthly. These substantially expand the represented domains and include univariate short-term forecasting. v3 has no corresponding evaluations; its descriptive PEMS04 mention is not equivalent coverage.

E2.justification: The main long-term comparator set is retained, but the fixed-96-input comparison involving TimeBridge, OLinear, TQNet, and CARD disappears. New Table 7 evaluates additional methods including FilterNet, FITS, TimeMixer++, Leddam, and Fredformer. Figure 13 also compares against TimeMixer on M4 and TimeMixer++ on PEMS.

E3.justification: v3's fixed-96-input, unified-hyperparameter evaluation is removed. v5 adds 36-input forecasting at horizons 24/36/48/60, PEMS comparisons using 96-input short horizons and 512-input long horizons, and M4 evaluation using SMAPE. These substantially change the evaluation designs represented, while the retained long-term benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 extends the two-component ablation to M4 and PEMS and measures how supervision gains vary across input/output horizons (Figure 13). This adds substantial evidence about when curriculum supervision helps. The earlier long-term component, depth, dropout, EMA, representation, and oracle-bound analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 2021 for the main experiments. v3 Table 9 and v5 Table 12 contain identical five-seed reporting, standard deviations, and 99% confidence entries for ReNF and TimeBridge, averaged across four horizons. No changed repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v5 adds extensive short-term and M4/PEMS results while removing the fixed-96-input results. For example, new Table 7 reports CarSales average ReNF MSE/MAE of 0.289/0.306. The main long-term tables are unchanged, but the retained component-ablation ETTh1 average MAE changes from 0.417 to 0.416. Figure 5 also reverses the EMA-condition attribution of unchanged curves.

T1.justification: v5 replaces MNFP's almost-sure convergence/l2 proposition with an absolute-error hypothesis, revises boundedness and independence assumptions, and modifies the accompanying derivation. It adds a covariance-based analysis of total forecast error in Appendix B.2 and a formal forecast-combination expression in Section 2.3. These are substantive mathematical changes despite retaining the bound's overall form.

C1.justification: The first-listed theoretical contribution in v3 becomes a variance-reduction hypothesis explicitly presented as qualitative motivation and is removed from the contribution list. v5 instead foregrounds the validation-test generalization gap and EMA's role in addressing it. The principal claims about BDO and efficient MLP forecasting performance remain.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges the mismatch between independent-candidate theory and recursive BDO, develops variance/covariance interpretations, and calls for explicit causal constraints. It carries the earlier noisy-short-input explanation into short-term evaluations and adds curriculum redundancy as a limitation supported by new ablations. The earlier ETTm2-specific weakness is no longer stated.

D1.justification: An explicit anonymous repository address replaces blank code placeholders in the abstract and reproducibility statement. v5 adds source descriptions and metadata for short-term datasets, while removing the explicit drop_last correction note and Figure 5's numerical EMA-decay labels. Hardware, optimizer, and principal hyperparameter-search disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Most of v3 Appendix A survives in v5 Section 4. v5 adds a more explicit comparison with N-BEATS/N-HiTS, distinguishing additive residual decomposition from recursive concatenation, and adds stacking, forecast-combination, EMA, DeepAR, and new-baseline references. These refine the existing research positioning; relocation itself is structural.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Design Space' to 'Principles'; the abstract, introduction, theoretical motivation, and contribution framing undergo substantial rewriting. Preliminary definitions are compressed, related work moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents list. The LLM-use declaration is removed.

P2.justification: v5 adds the multipart Figure 13 and short-term Table 7, removes v3 Table 6, expands the dataset table, and reformats several appendix tables, including transposing the dropout results. Captions and legends also change, including the reversed EMA labels in Figure 5. Most existing diagrams and plots are reused.

improvement.justification: v5 better documents applicability boundaries through short-term evaluations and M4/PEMS ablations, explicitly acknowledges the theory's independence limitation, and supplies a concrete code-access address. These improve assessment and reproducibility of the work. The gain is limited by removing the fixed-96-input comparison and reversing Figure 5's EMA labels: v3's zero-decay blue curve becomes 'with EMA' in v5. The principal long-term results and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
